glosses: Employer sur une personne les procédés indiqués par les adeptes de la doctrine appelée magnétisme.

examples.text: Il est certain que si l'on persuade à un « bon sujet » qu'une cliche de porte est magnétisée, au moment où il avancera la main pour ouvrir la porte il tombera en hypnotisme.

Madame Fontaine, qui prédit l’avenir huit fois sur dix, n’a jamais su qu’elle perdrait sa mise à la loterie.
— Il en est ainsi en magnétisme, fit observer Bixiou. L’on ne se magnétise pas soi-même.
Ses yeux allaient de l'une à l'autre comme s'il essayait de les magnétiser.

glosses: Transmettre des propriétés magnétiques à un objet.
Produire, avoir une forte attraction sur des personnes.

examples.text: S’il a récolté autant de votes, il le doit au gourou fou qu’il a choisi à sa tête. Son charisme a magnétisé beaucoup d’Américains qui ne comprennent pas bien les enjeux réels de leur pays. Le programme du parti s’est transformé en un culte de Trump.

translations.source_sense_description: Employer sur une personne les procédés indiqués par les adeptes de la doctrine appelée magnétisme.

glosses: To exercise mesmerism on; to affect another person, such as to heal or soothe, through the use of animal magnetism.

examples.text: Mesmer had about a hundred people whom he had instructed as magnetisers, some of whom belonged to the nobility, who also "mesmerised" people by making passes over the affected parts of the body.
She mesmerized the audience with her tricks

Then he commenced to talk, really talk, and inside of two flaps of a herring’s fin he had me mesmerized, like Eben Holt’s boy at the town hall show. He talked about the ills of humanity, and the glories of health and Nature and service and land knows what all.

examples.text: There is, we fear, a tendency to be mesmerised by the glamour of something new and to refrain from the cold hard look that monorail concepts deserve.

examples.text:
c. 1789, Elizabeth Inchbald, Animal Magnetism: A Farce, Dublin, P. Byron, Act III, p. 82,
Lisette let him alone, it is dangerous to push the poor creature to extremities, Doctor, suppose we Magnetize him?

Dr. Bertrand tells us that the first patient he ever magnetized, being attacked by a disease of an hysterical character, became subject to convulsions of so long duration and so violent in character, that he had never, in all his practice, seen the like […]

glosses: To attract, allure or entice; to captivate or entrance.

examples.text: As for Dudley Venner, no beauty in all the world could have so soothed and magnetized him as the very repose and subdued gentleness which the Widow had thought would make the best possible background for her own more salient and effective attractions.
Mr. Hamlin’s hand passed carressingly twice or thrice along her sleeve with a peculiar gentleness that seemed to magnetize her.
Subdued and magnetized into submission, Ursula sat turning her tearful eyes from one uncompromising face to the other; but their attention was soon diverted to another weeper.

Drawing his material from the black hole of ghetto life and death, Pryor uses his dramatic power to magnetize his listeners into the fire-flash fear of the moment—even as his skewed comic perspective offers distance, safety, reassurance.
